newsitem.title: USA: NBA-JORDAN NAMED TO ALL-DEFENSIVE FIRST TEAM FOR EIGHTH TIME.
newsitem.headline: NBA-JORDAN NAMED TO ALL-DEFENSIVE FIRST TEAM FOR EIGHTH TIME.

text.p: Chicago Bulls superstar Michael Jordan, the perennial league-leader in scoring, was named to the NBA All-Defensive First Team for a record-tying eighth time, the National Basketball Association announced on Tuesday.
Only former Philadelphia and Denver star Bobby Jones was selected to as many NBA All-Defensive teams as Jordan, who was named on the maximum 28 ballots in voting by the league's 29 head coaches.

Joining Jordan on the 1996-97 NBA All-Defensive First Team were Atlanta centre Dikembe Mutombo, who last week was named NBA Defensive Player of the Year, Seattle guard Gary Payton, who was last year's Defensive Player of the Year, Chicago forward Scottie Pippen and Utah forward Karl Malone.

The NBA All-Defensive Second Team consisted of Charlotte's Anthony Mason and Miami's P.J. Brown at forward, Houston's Hakeem Olajuwon at centre and Atlanta's Mookie Blaylock and Utah's John Stockton at guard.

Pippen led all players in the voting, picking up 26 first-team votes and 53 points. Jordan, who was second with 23 first-team votes and 51 points, and Payton were the only players named on the maximum 28 ballots.
Two points were awarded for a first team vote and one for a second team selection. Coaches were not permitted to vote for players from their own team.
Pippen received the defensive accolade for the sixth time, and Payton for the fourth, while Mutombo and Malone were newcomers to the NBA All-Defensive First Team.
